transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Amira Johnson (BlueWave VP Eng), Raj Patel (BlueWave SRE), Sofia Martinez (Product), Ethan Cole (Security)

Summary: POC weekly - focus on rollout/go-live planning, cutover sequencing, canary/A-B options, monitoring & runbook items.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — cutover plan, canary vs A/B, monitoring/alerts, runbooks, and open security items. We're about 45 minutes, so we'll try to be crisp.

[00:18] Amira Johnson: Sounds good. We want to make sure whatever we do doesn't spike latency for our front-line users. Our SLA target is p95 < 350ms for chat endpoints.

[00:34] Marco Chen: Right, p95 350ms target noted. For the POC we've been running Redwood Dedicated in your staging region with the default batching settings, and average tail latency has been around 220-260ms. There were a couple of bursts that pushed p99 higher though.

[00:52] Raj Patel: Those bursts correlate with some background jobs hitting the same GPU nodes, we think. We'll share the job schedules. Also, we want to confirm how Redwood's smart routing handles capacity burst fallback - is that automatic?

[01:07] Marco Chen: Good question. Smart routing can fallback to a secondary model variant or region based on your policy. For the POC we set up a simple fallback to a quantized variant with slightly lower token quality but much lower cost/latency. We can tweak rules so only certain routes use fallback.

[01:29] Sofia Martinez: For product we were thinking of an A/B test for the new summarization flow - maybe 20% of traffic to model B for 2 weeks, compare accuracy metrics. Does that complicate the rollout?

[01:43] Lena Park: Not really. We typically recommend a canary first for infra cutover - like 1% then 5% then 20% - to validate infra and metrics. A/B for feature comparison can run in parallel but keep canary focused on infra stability.

[02:03] Amira Johnson: Can you walk us through the cutover sequence you recommend? Step-by-step?

[02:12] Marco Chen: Yeah. Our suggested cutover runbook high-level:
- Pre-cutover checks (health of nodes, KV cache warm, model weights pinned)
- Deploy canary: route 1% of production traffic for 1 hour, monitor latency, error rate, token-cost delta
- If green, move to 5% for 2 hours; then 20% for 4 hours; then 100% with fast rollback gates at each stage
- Post-cutover: continuous monitoring for 72 hours and compare scoring/eval buckets for quality regressions

[02:46] Priya Rao: We'll include checklist items like verifying KV cache priming and ensuring prewarming is complete. Also adding log ship tests to confirm audit logs land in your SIEM.

[03:01] Ethan Cole: On logs - we need to ensure audit logs include per-request IDs and redwood-run id so we can correlate user requests. Also KMS key policies: do you support customer-managed keys?

[03:12] Marco Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated with integration options for HSM. There may be a few config steps - we'll put the details in the runbook.

[03:25] Amira Johnson: Regarding monitoring: what dashboards/alerts should we expect out of Redwood Console for the canary?

[03:34] Lena Park: We'll provide a pre-built dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost per request, cache hit ratio, throughput (RPS), and inference CPU/GPU utilization. Alerts: p95 breach, error-rate spike >0.5% over baseline, and token-cost variance >20% for a route.

[03:58] Raj Patel: Who owns the alert -> pager? We need to wire alerts to our SRE team.

[04:05] Priya Rao: We'll help map Redwood alerts into your PagerDuty - we just need the escalation policy and team channel.

[04:14] Sofia Martinez: On canary sizing: we shared expected QPS in the doc but maybe not broken down by route. For canary, do you need absolute request counts or percentages?

[04:27] Marco Chen: Absolute counts are helpful for capacity planning - 1% of a 1,000 QPS endpoint is still 10 QPS, which matters for cold-start behavior. Please send both.

[04:40] Amira Johnson: We'll put together the top 20 routes with QPS by Friday.

[04:47] Ethan Cole: A security note - audit logs retention and who can access them. We need SOC 2 style retention for 90 days in the control plane and long-term in your archive if possible.

[05:00] Lena Park: Understood. We have built-in audit logs and can configure retention. For Private customers we can also set up a customer-managed retention policy. We'll include options in the security appendix of the runbook.

[05:15] Raj Patel: What about rollback times? If something goes wrong at 20% canary, how fast can we revert to previous model?

[05:23] Marco Chen: The platform supports instant traffic re-routing - effectively seconds to flip. But we recommend an automated rollback gate that can be triggered by an alert or runbook step; operator confirmation is typical for production.

[05:36] Amira Johnson: Are there any known regressions when switching from quantized variant back to full-precision? We worry about a sudden quality jump confusing users.

[05:46] Marco Chen: Good point. You can mitigate by using model-variant tagging and running a gradual sweep, or using response metadata to annotate which variant responded so product can smooth the user experience. We'll include a UX suggestion in the playbook.

[06:02] Sofia Martinez: For the A/B experiment I want to make sure eval hooks are in place - we need reference prompt sets and automated sampling to compare quality metrics.

[06:12] Priya Rao: Redwood Optimize can run bucketed evals and alert on regressions vs baseline. We'll set up an eval job to run continuously on sampled traffic and surface any quality drops.

[06:22] Raj Patel: Can you show the exact metrics Redwood Console will surface for the canary?

[06:28] Marco Chen: Yes - we'll share a dashboard screenshot. It includes time-series for latency percentiles, error rate, token cost, and a small table of sample outputs with similarity scores. Note: transcription earlier had a mislabel where KV cache was spelled 'KV cash' in our docs, ignore that.

[06:47] Amira Johnson: Security question - is there an option to restrict model weights from being copied out in logs? We need to ensure no model artifacts leak to logs.

[06:57] Ethan Cole: Right, we need to redact model internals and ensure no sensitive user data is stored in logs.

[07:04] Marco Chen: Audit logs do not contain model weights. Request/response logs can be configured to redact or exclude full-response bodies. We'll provide guidance on minimal logging policy for compliance.

[07:18] Lena Park: Ok, let's talk schedule. We're aiming for a staged go-live mid-November. Feels like two weeks for final prep. Proposed timeline: runbook & canary config by 11/02, staging dry-run 11/09, production canary start 11/16, full cutover 11/20 if all green. Thoughts?

[07:37] Amira Johnson: That timeline could work as long as we get the cutover runbook and the traffic numbers this week. Also need a security sign-off before production canary.

[07:48] Ethan Cole: We'll need two security checkpoints - after runbook review and after the staging dry-run where we validate telemetry and KMS integration.

[07:58] Marco Chen: Makes sense. We'll mark those as hard gates in the runbook.

[08:04] Sofia Martinez: Any concerns around cost spikes during canary? Token cost could increase if we accidentally route heavier prompts to the higher-cost model.

[08:14] Marco Chen: We'll include cost guardrails - per-route token budget alarms and an automatic throttle if cost per 5-minute window exceeds threshold. Also recommend a traffic label so we can isolate experimental traffic.

[08:29] Raj Patel: Is the KV cache priming going to be manual or automatic during cutover? We saw cold cache during an earlier test.

[08:36] Marco Chen: We recommend a priming step prior to canary: run a synthetic replay of recent traffic to warm the KV cache. We have a tooling script to do that; we'll include it in the runbook.

[08:47] Amira Johnson: Ok, please add that script to the runbook repo.

[08:53] Marco Chen: Will do.

[08:58] Priya Rao: A couple logistics - who will be the on-call Redwood person during the cutover? Lena? Marco?

[09:05] Lena Park: Marco will be primary SE for the cutover, I'll be AE owner and Priya will coordinate post-cutover analysis. We'll include contact info in the runbook.

[09:16] Ethan Cole: For KMS: can Redwood key operations be audited? We need a chain of custody.

[09:22] Marco Chen: Yes, KMS operations can be forwarded to your audit log. For Private deployments we can also integrate with your HSM vendor for key custody.

[09:34] Amira Johnson: Let's recap next steps quickly.

[09:38] Lena Park: Recap - Redwood will: 1) share cutover runbook and canary playbook by 11/02, 2) provide dashboard and cost guardrail configs, 3) share KV priming script, 4) document KMS integration steps. BlueWave will: 1) share top 20 routes + QPS by 11/04, 2) provide PagerDuty escalation policy, 3) security will review runbook and return comments.

[10:00] Raj Patel: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the traffic numbers by Friday.

[10:06] Lena Park: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send the runbook draft and schedule the staging dry-run slot.

[10:10] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels may be imperfect and a few words transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'KV cash' vs 'KV cache', 'redwood-run id' rather than consistent request ids).
